free_tier.stated: Each project in a Free tier namespace on GitLab.com has 10 GiB of free storage for the project's repository and LFS. A project in a Premium or Ultimate tier has 500 GiB. The container registry, package registry and build artifacts are not included in the limit. Whether snippets, uploads and wikis count: unverified, the page does not say.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-object limit for Git LFS objects is stated on the pages read. Related limits: git push and project imports are limited to 5 GiB for each request through Cloudflare; maximum attachment size is 100 MiB.
per_object_cap.notes: The GitLab.com limits page lists a maximum push size of 5 GiB and a maximum attachment size of 100 MiB; it lists no separate Git LFS object size.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: When a project's repository and LFS exceed the 10 GiB limit, the project is set to a read-only state. No expiry period for repository or LFS storage is stated on the page.

egress.terms: unverified: no egress charge or volume quota is stated on the pages read. The only transfer-side control stated is a request rate: on GitLab.com Git LFS requests are subject to the authenticated web request rate limit of 1000 requests per minute per user, and each Git LFS object uploaded or downloaded generates one HTTP request.

tooling: git-lfs. Also Oras-style raw access is not available; LFS is protocol-only. GitLab REST API v4 for project/namespace management (useful for automating project-per-shard).
chaining: Each project in a Free tier namespace on GitLab.com has its own 10 GiB of free storage for the project's repository and LFS. The number of projects allowed per namespace or account: unverified, the pages read state no limit and no cap.
limits_note: At 10 GiB the project goes READ-ONLY: 'you can't push or add large files (LFS) to the project's repository.' Max push request 5 GiB (through Cloudflare). This applies to git push; LFS object upload is a separate endpoint. Max attachment 100 MiB. Rate limit 1000 LFS req/min/user is the real throughput ceiling (~60k objects/hour, and one object = one request regardless of size).

reliability_note: Read-only state is reversible only by purchasing storage, so a blown project is stuck. The 1000 req/min limit bites hard on many-small-files datasets during clone, and GitLab's own docs warn multi-file projects 'may encounter an HTTP rate limit error' in CI.

extras.quota_verbatim: 10 GiB free storage PER PROJECT on the Free tier, and that 10 GiB explicitly covers 'the project's repository and Large File Storage (LFS)'. Premium/Ultimate: 500 GiB per project. CONFIRMED: LFS is IN the quota while containers, packages, build artifacts, snippets, uploads and wikis are OUT.
extras.limits_verbatim: At 10 GiB the project goes READ-ONLY: 'you can't push or add large files (LFS) to the project's repository.' Max push request 5 GiB (through Cloudflare) — this applies to git push; LFS object upload is a separate endpoint. Max attachment 100 MiB. Rate limit 1000 LFS req/min/user is the real throughput ceiling (~60k objects/hour, and one object = one request regardless of size).
extras.egress_verbatim: Unmetered — GitLab does not bill or publish any LFS bandwidth quota. The only transfer-side control is a rate limit: 'Git LFS requests are subject to authenticated web request rate limits ... 1000 requests per minute per user. Each Git LFS object uploaded or downloaded generates an HTTP request'.
extras.chaining_verbatim: 10 GiB per PROJECT, and projects are free and unlimited within a namespace — GitLab's own excess-storage example totals 30 GiB across three projects with no namespace-level cap. 50 projects = 500 GiB, 100 = 1 TiB. This is the cleanest 'trivially repeatable' LFS case because each project is an independent 10 GiB bucket behind the same account, unlike GitHub where the 10 GiB is per account.
extras.tooling_verbatim: git-lfs. Also Oras-style raw access is not available; LFS is protocol-only. GitLab REST API v4 for project/namespace management (useful for automating project-per-shard).
